title: census.py phase1_commit finds a one-domain census's phase-1 commit, so sample --brief reads its keys
goal: census.phase1_commit(D) finds the phase-1 verdicts commit of a census of one domain (subject 'census D <domain> phase 1 verdicts') as well as a whole-kb one, so sample --brief's 'unchanged since phase 1' reads that commit's keys. Found by the SP-htl7jkrm review: the 2026-10-11 logs census was committed as 'census 2026-10-11 logs phase 1 verdicts' and phase1_commit('2026-10-11') returns '' (_tools/census.py:1274), so every same-day phase-1 anchor goes to the checker.

run:
import sys, os, tempfile, subprocess, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import census, kbcommon
ENV = dict(os.environ, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='a', GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='a@example.com', GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='a', GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='a@example.com')
t = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()
g = lambda *a: subprocess.run(['git', *a], cwd=t, env=ENV, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
g('init', '-q', '-b', 'main')
(t/'f').write_text('1'); g('add', '-A'); g('commit', '-q', '-m', 'docs(kb): census 2026-10-11 logs phase 1 verdicts')
sha = g('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
(t/'f').write_text('2'); g('add', '-A'); g('commit', '-q', '-m', 'docs(kb): census 2026-10-12 phase 1 verdicts')
kbcommon.HOME = t
sys.exit(0 if census.phase1_commit('2026-10-11') == sha else 1)
